verdict.rationale: LiveKit's core media server is open source and documented as easy to self-deploy as a single binary, Docker image, or Kubernetes deployment, with a dev mode and self-hosting networking docs. The docs explicitly support moving between self-hosted and LiveKit Cloud, and a community team describes it as an SFU you run yourself. Missing for 10: in-depth self-hosting production deployment guidance in the pack beyond ports and firewall, and clarity on parity for Cloud-only features such as Inference, Agent Builder, and Phone Numbers.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Easy to deploy: single binary, Docker or Kubernetes
You can move from LiveKit Cloud to self-hosted if your requirements change.
You can start on open source and migrate to LiveKit Cloud without rewriting application code.
They called it the right choice for a modern SFU you run yourself.
It's possible to handle all UDP traffic on a single port.
